note: Defects injected into the generated PostgreSQL shop to prove the ecommerce contention criteria can actually fail. A criterion in tracks/ecommerce/scenarios/01-contention.json stays at zero points until it CATCHES its mutant here and still passes on the unmutated build. Anchors are specific to this app; regenerate for another. NOTE: breaks must be the numeric FEATURE id — mutation-test.mjs indexes per-feature scores; a criterion id silently resolves to undefined and every mutant reads as SURVIVED.

mutations.desc: Drop FOR UPDATE from the stock read in the purchase transaction, so concurrent buyers each see the same pre-decrement quantity, both pass the availability check, and the shelf goes below zero or sells the last unit twice

edits.find: `SELECT id, quantity FROM item_stock WHERE item_id = $1 ORDER BY warehouse_id FOR UPDATE`
edits.replace: `SELECT id, quantity FROM item_stock WHERE item_id = $1 ORDER BY warehouse_id`

mutations.desc: DISCARDED — EQUIVALENT MUTANT. Rewriting `quantity = quantity + N` as a subselect against the same row is semantically identical in PostgreSQL: both read the row's current version under the statement's snapshot, so nothing observable changes. It proved nothing, and an equivalent mutant is indistinguishable from an oracle hole. A real lost update needs the read and the write split across two statements with the value carried in application memory.

edits.find: `UPDATE item_stock SET quantity = quantity + $1 WHERE item_id = $2 AND warehouse_id = $3
edits.replace: `UPDATE item_stock SET quantity = (SELECT quantity FROM item_stock s WHERE s.item_id = $2 AND s.warehouse_id = $3) + $1 WHERE item_id = $2 AND warehouse_id = $3
